sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Growth was steady in the mid-teens until FY2023, when it slowed to 6.9%, then reaccelerated to 17.8% in FY2026 [D311][D472].
The FY2026 step-up came from Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud revenue up 29.7% on Azure demand [D916][P17][P12].
The FY2018 dip in net income to $16.6 billion was a tax event, the net charge from enactment of the TCJA [F52][P61].
Microsoft Cloud reached 64.6% of revenue in FY2026 and contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% growth [D566][D568][D472].
Server products and cloud services grew 31.5% to $129.4 billion, driven by Azure and other cloud services [S61][D641][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added $14.2 billion, or 16%, on Copilot and E5 revenue per user [P14].
Operating income grew 20.8% against revenue growth of 17.8%, an incremental margin of 53.3% [D473][D472][D498].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against net income growth of 31.3%, with the share count down only 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% is a window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin fell 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as AI infrastructure investment raised cost of revenue [F30][D486][D981][P11].
Cost of revenue took 0.9pp off operating margin, while R&D leverage added 0.8pp as R&D fell to 10.7% of revenue [D500][D501][D450].
Operating expenses rose 7.4% on AI compute, AI talent and XBOX impairment, well below revenue growth [D491][P16].
Net margin rose 4.2pp to 40.3%, helped by $6.5 billion of OpenAI investment gains in other income [F70][D488][P7].
Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income, in line with the 1.34x median [F100][F60][D459][D1013].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion, a 20.2% margin and window low, as capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion [F120][D478][D456][D982][F110][D479].
The capex increase was $51.4 billion of additions to property and equipment, plus $22.2 billion of other investing for components [P1].
Capex ran at 3.38x D&A and 34.9% of revenue, against 8.4% of revenue in FY2017 [D461][D455][D7].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, or 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers [D465][D466][D1006].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion while cash and investments rose 2.9% to $113.2 billion [D464][D495][D463][D494].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion and dividends of $26.4 billion used 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468].
The current ratio of 1.23x is a window low against a 1.93x median, as current liabilities grew 19.5% [F200][D991][D993][D485].
Free cash flow fell to 0.50x net income, a window low and 20th percentile against a 1.90x peer median [D460][D988][D1008][D1009].
The gap is capex-driven, with additions to property and equipment up $51.4 billion, not a working-capital problem [P1].
Free cash flow margin of 20.2% sits far below the 34.7% peer median, so the cash profile now lags the profit profile [D456][D1003].
FY2017 short-term investments were not reported, so cash and net cash for that year omit them and cross-gap comparisons are unreliable [R6][X158].
Capex at 34.9% of revenue is the key variable; a move back toward the FY2025 level of 22.9% would restore free cash flow [D455][D401].
Watch whether operating margin holds above the 41.7% median as AI infrastructure costs keep pressuring gross margin [D975][F30].
Watch Microsoft Cloud's 64.6% revenue share and 26.9% growth; a slowdown below the FY2025 rate of 22.7% would mark a reversal [D566][D567][D564].
